title: Driver-placed claims get a lease capped at the dispatch deadline (#879)

story.i_want_to: a claim placed for a runner dispatch to expire at the dispatch's deadline plus a grace
story.so_that: a killed session releases its story within minutes, not 23 hours, and no other claimant is affected

rationale: The lease is one global 24h value against a 3600s wall clock, so a killed session holds its story for most of a day. Lowering the global value breaks every non-runner claimant. A per-claim cap derived from the dispatch fixes the one population the runner hard-kills, and sharing the instant with the runner closes the window where two sessions could work one story.

acceptance_criteria.description: A claim Placement takes for a runner dispatch has claimed_until = placed_at + wall_clock_seconds + DISPATCH_LEASE_GRACE_SECONDS.
Renewing a driver-placed claim never moves claimed_until past that cap.
A claim taken through claim_story/3 or bulk_claim/4 outside placement keeps claim_lease_seconds/0 exactly as today.
The application refuses to boot with DISPATCH_LEASE_GRACE_SECONDS below Capacity.release_grace_seconds/0.
The implement dispatch payload carries deadline_at equal to the claim's cap minus the grace.
The renew_story_claim tool description and mcp-server/README.md state that driver-placed claims are capped at the dispatch deadline.

test_cases.name: placed claim carries the cap
preconditions: runner, contracted story, wall clock 3600, grace 900

test_cases.name: renewal cannot extend past the cap
grace below release grace refuses boot

technical_notes: Lease today: Progress.claim_lease_seconds/0 and claim_lease_change/2 (progress.ex:1315,1329), used by claim_story/3 and bulk_claim/4
Placement: lib/loopctl/delivery/placement.ex; store the cap on the claim so renewal can read it (the dispatch row already carries wall_clock_seconds)
non_goals: Does not change the global lease
Does not fence git pushes by epoch (delivery-authority work)
